observation.visible_scene: An outdoor dusk setting with a small low wooden table on dry grass. In front of the table sit two upright cardboard-tube cylinders; a small box is partly visible beneath the table, and a thin white cord lies on the ground to the left. Tall weeds and a tree line the left background. A large, intensely bright white-yellow flame core sits on the tabletop, enveloped by a voluminous billowing smoke cloud lit orange on its upper surfaces and pale gray on the right.
visible_changes: The bright flame core on the table persists throughout but gradually shrinks in area and shifts toward the left edge of the tabletop, becoming a smaller elongated orange glow by the end of the segment.

The surrounding smoke cloud continuously expands upward and outward, rising diagonally to the upper left and spreading to the right, growing so large that it fills most of the upper frame and increasingly obscures the background.
The smoke's coloration changes from strongly orange-lit near the flame in the early frames to a more diffuse grayish-white as it rises and cools.
Numerous small bright sparks/embers are ejected and scatter around the table and into the left and right portions of the frame, appearing as discrete dots that persist and drift.

The table, the two cylinders, the box under the table, and the white cord remain stationary in fixed positions relative to the frame; the background tree and weeds do not move, indicating no camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: The ignition event or trigger that started the combustion before t=0 is not shown.
The identity of the burning material on the table and the source of the smoke are not visible.
The eventual dissipation of the smoke and extinguishing of the flame after t=2.67 s are not shown.
uncertain_details: Whether the leftward migration of the bright core reflects fuel consumption across the surface or occlusion by rising smoke is not determinable.
The exact nature of the ejected sparks (burning fragments vs. embers) cannot be confirmed.
Minor apparent jitter of the smoke edges between adjacent frames is consistent with turbulent expansion rather than camera shake.
